title: Flood / overland flow / storm tide
code: Flood overlay code
note: Part of the lot is mapped in a flood planning area. Minimum habitable floor levels, flood-resilient design and limits on filling and intensification are likely to apply.
checklist: Order a Council FloodWise Property Report for flood levels
Confirm the flood planning area category and minimum habitable floor level
Check whether filling or excavation is needed and its flood impacts

title: Heritage
code: Heritage overlay code
note: The lot is on, or adjoins, a heritage place or pre-1911 building. Demolition and building work can trigger assessment and heritage impact requirements.
checklist: Check the Local Heritage Places register and the Queensland Heritage Register citation
Assess whether a heritage impact statement is needed
Note that any state heritage place is referred to SARA

title: Character protection
code: Traditional building character overlay code / Dwelling house character overlay code / Commercial character building overlay code
note: Character controls restrict demolition or removal of older buildings and require new work to respect the streetscape.
checklist: Establish the house's construction date (pre-1947 is relevant)
Check whether demolition or removal needs approval
Review the design requirements for new work and extensions

title: Bushfire hazard
code: Bushfire overlay code
note: The lot is in a mapped bushfire hazard area. Separation, access and building construction standards (AS 3959) may apply.
checklist: Confirm the hazard level
Obtain a BAL assessment (AS 3959)
Check the access and water supply requirements

title: Landslide / steep land
code: Landslide overlay code
note: Mapped landslide or steep land hazard. A geotechnical assessment is likely to be required.
checklist: Commission a geotechnical report
Minimise cut and fill and retaining walls

title: Acid sulfate soils
code: Potential and actual acid sulfate soils overlay code
note: Excavation or filling may disturb acid sulfate soils. Testing and a management plan may be required.
checklist: Check excavation depth against the mapped thresholds
Arrange soil testing if excavation is proposed

title: Biodiversity / waterways / vegetation
code: Biodiversity areas overlay code / Waterway corridors overlay code / Wetlands overlay code / Significant landscape tree overlay code
note: Ecological values are mapped on the lot. Vegetation clearing, setbacks from waterways and ecological assessment may be required, and state koala mapping may also apply.
checklist: Map vegetation and waterways on site
Check clearing restrictions and protected vegetation
Check the state koala habitat mapping (SPP / Queensland Globe)

title: Airport environs
code: Airport environs overlay code
note: Height limits (obstacle limitation surfaces), aircraft noise (ANEF) or lighting and wildlife controls may apply.
checklist: Check the building height against the OLS
Check the ANEF contour for noise attenuation

title: Transport noise / air quality
code: Transport noise corridor overlay code / Transport air quality corridor overlay code
note: The lot is near a major road or rail corridor. Acoustic treatment of the building (QDC MP4.4) and air quality design may be required.
checklist: Identify the noise category
Allow for the cost of acoustic glazing and construction

title: Road, transport and infrastructure networks
code: Road hierarchy overlay code / Streetscape hierarchy overlay code / Critical infrastructure and movement network overlay code
note: Frontage roads, access, streetscape treatment and infrastructure corridors can affect driveway location, setbacks and works requirements.
checklist: Confirm the road hierarchy of each frontage
Check access and driveway constraints
Check for any infrastructure easements or corridors

title: Industrial amenity / extractive resources
code: Industrial amenity overlay code / Extractive resources overlay code
note: Nearby industry or extractive resources may limit sensitive uses or require separation and amenity mitigation.
checklist: Identify nearby industry or quarries and their buffers

title: Coastal hazard
code: Coastal hazard overlay code
note: Coastal erosion or storm tide inundation hazards are mapped on the lot.
checklist: Check the erosion prone area and storm tide levels

title: Neighbourhood plan
code: Neighbourhood plan code (the relevant plan)
note: A neighbourhood plan applies. It can change the levels of assessment, building heights and the uses supported compared with the base zone.
checklist: Read the neighbourhood plan code and its precinct for this lot
Check the neighbourhood plan's tables of assessment

title: Active frontages
code: Active frontages in residential zones overlay code
note: Ground-level activation of the street frontage may be required.
checklist: Plan for ground-floor street activation

title: Within 25 m of a state-controlled road
code: Planning Regulation 2017, Schedule 10 (state transport infrastructure); State Development Assessment Provisions (SDAP) state code for development in a state-controlled road environment
note: The lot is within 25 m of a state-controlled road. A material change of use, reconfiguring a lot or operational work may need referral to SARA, with the Department of Transport and Main Roads advising. Conditions can cover access, stormwater, noise and road works.
checklist: Check SARA DA mapping (state-controlled road layers)
Confirm whether access is from the state-controlled road
Allow for a pre-lodgement meeting with SARA

title: SEQ koala habitat
code: Planning Regulation 2017, Schedules 10 and 11 (SEQ koala habitat); SDAP state code for development in SEQ koala habitat areas
note: State koala mapping applies. Clearing koala habitat where a koala priority area and a koala habitat area overlap is generally prohibited. Other clearing or development can trigger SARA referral.
checklist: Survey for koala habitat trees
Check whether the lot is in both a koala priority area and a koala habitat area
Design to avoid clearing mapped habitat

title: Wetland protection area / HES wetland
code: Planning Regulation 2017, Schedule 10 (wetland protection areas); SDAP wetland state code
note: Earthworks or development in or near a mapped wetland can trigger SARA referral and buffer requirements.
checklist: Confirm the wetland boundary and trigger area
Plan buffers to the wetland

title: Regulated native vegetation
code: Planning Regulation 2017, Schedule 10 (clearing native vegetation); Vegetation Management Act 1999; SDAP native vegetation clearing state code
note: Regulated vegetation or essential habitat is mapped on the lot. Clearing for a material change of use or reconfiguring a lot can trigger SARA referral and offsets.
checklist: Confirm the regulated vegetation category (A, B, C or R)
Check whether a PMAV applies
Avoid or minimise clearing

title: Coastal management district / erosion prone area / storm tide
code: Planning Regulation 2017, Schedule 10 (coastal protection); Coastal Protection and Management Act 1995; SDAP coastal development state code
note: Coastal mapping applies. Building, tidal works or reconfiguring a lot may trigger SARA referral, and storm tide hazard affects floor levels.
checklist: Check the erosion prone area width
Check the storm tide hazard and minimum floor levels

title: Priority Development Area
code: Economic Development Act 2012; relevant PDA development scheme (Economic Development Queensland)
note: The site is in a PDA. The PDA development scheme replaces City Plan for development assessment, and EDQ is usually the assessment manager. Council's City Plan zone is for reference only.
checklist: Download the PDA development scheme and its land-use plan
Identify the precinct and its height and density provisions
Book a pre-lodgement meeting with EDQ

title: SEQ Regional Plan (ShapingSEQ 2023)
code: ShapingSEQ 2023; Planning Regulation 2017, Schedule 12 (regional landscape and rural production area)
note: Check the land use category. Urban Footprint supports urban development, while the Regional Landscape and Rural Production Area strictly limits urban uses and subdivision.
checklist: Confirm the regional land use category

title: Protected plants trigger area (DESI)
code: Nature Conservation Act 1992 — protected plants framework
note: Clearing native plants here may need a flora survey and a clearing permit from the Department of the Environment, Tourism, Science and Innovation.
checklist: Commission a protected plants flora survey before clearing

title: Federal EPBC Act (koala)
code: Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation Act 1999 (Cth)
note: The koala is a nationally listed threatened species. A significant impact on koala habitat may need referral to the Australian Government, separate from council and SARA.
checklist: Assess whether a significant impact is likely (EPBC self-assessment)

title: Airport / federal airspace
code: Airports Act 1996 (Cth); Airports (Protection of Airspace) Regulations
note: Buildings or cranes that penetrate prescribed airspace need federal approval through the airport operator.
checklist: Check building and crane heights against the prescribed airspace

title: Water and sewer (Urban Utilities)
code: South East Queensland Water (Distribution and Retail Restructuring) Act 2009 — Urban Utilities connections
note: New or intensified development needs water and sewer connection approval from Urban Utilities and may attract infrastructure charges.
checklist: Request an Urban Utilities connection or services advice
Check for sewer mains through the lot (build-over rules)

title: Electricity and services
code: Energex supply requirements; Before You Dig Australia
note: Check easements, overhead lines, substations and service locations before design.
checklist: Lodge a Before You Dig enquiry
Check the title for easements

title: Easements
code: Title search / registered plan
note: An easement is mapped over part of the lot. Easements (for example drainage, sewer, access or power) can restrict building, fencing, landscaping and subdivision layout. The map shows where; the title search shows the purpose and who benefits.
checklist: Order a title search and read each easement's purpose and beneficiary
Check whether the easement is held by the water and sewer provider, Energex, Council or a neighbour
Keep buildings and deep structures clear of the easement unless the holder consents
Show the easement on all plans lodged with the application
